s: What does Ashoka's title 'Devanampiya' mean?
x: Devanampiya means 'Beloved of the Gods'; Piyadasi means 'of gracious mien' and Amitraghata 'slayer of foes'.

s: In which year was the Maski edict, which carries the name 'Ashoka', found?
x: The Maski edict was found in 1915; 1837 is Prinsep's decipherment and 1793 Jones's identification.

s: In which two minor rock edicts does the personal name 'Ashoka' occur?
x: The name Ashoka appears in the Maski and Gujarra minor rock edicts.

s: Which Ashokan edicts were the first to be read by James Prinsep?
x: The Delhi-Topra pillar edicts were the first Ashokan edicts to be read.

s: Most Ashokan edicts call the king only 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'. In which pair of edicts does the personal name 'Ashoka' appear?
x: The name Ashoka occurs in the Maski (Raichur, Karnataka) and Gujarra (Madhya Pradesh) minor rock edicts (APPSC-G1 2022). Girnar and Kalsi carry the 14 Major Rock Edicts, Dhauli and Jaugada the Separate Kalinga Edicts, and Delhi-Topra and Rummindei are pillar inscriptions, all using the title Devanampiya Piyadasi.

s: Which title of Ashoka is associated with the Bhabru or Bairat Inscription?
x: The Bhabru (Bairat) inscription calls Ashoka "Piyadasi Raja" of Magadha and declares his faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha. Param Saugat was Dharmapala's title and Sikandar-i-Sani Alauddin Khalji's.

s: What does 'Devanampiya' mean in Ashoka's title Devanampiya Piyadasi?
x: 'Beloved of the Gods' translates Devanampiya, while Piyadasi (Priyadarshi) means 'of gracious appearance'.

s:
Consider the following about the Kanaganahalli inscription:
1. It is located in Karnataka.
2. It is associated with the Bhima river.
3. It contains the words 'Ranyo Ashoka'.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Kanaganahalli lies in Karnataka on the Bhima river and carries a portrait panel labelled 'Ranyo Ashoka'.

s: In which year was the Maski edict, which confirmed that Devanampiya Piyadasi was Ashoka, found?
x: The Maski edict, found in 1915, named Ashoka and so confirmed his identification with Devanampiya Piyadasi.

s: In which year did James Prinsep decipher the Brahmi script?
x: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837.

s: The form of Ashoka's edicts, including the word 'lipi/dipi', follows the inscriptions of which Persian king?
x: Ashoka's edict form, moving from third to first person and using 'lipi/dipi', follows Darius's inscriptions.

s: Who was the first ruler in India to inscribe messages to his subjects and officials on rocks and polished pillars?
x: Ashoka was the first ruler to address his people through inscriptions on natural rocks and polished stone pillars.

s: By which name is Ashoka called in the Maski edict?
x: The Maski edict calls him 'Buddhashakya Ashoka'; Dharmasoka is from Sarnath, Piyadasi Raja from Bhabru and Ashok Vardhan from the Puranas.

s: Which Ashokan edict bans animal slaughter and sacrifice?
x: RE I bans slaughter and sacrifice; RE II deals with medical treatment.

s: How many Major Rock Edicts did Ashoka issue?
x: Ashoka issued 14 Major Rock Edicts, found complete at sites like Girnar and Kalsi.

s: Which Yavana (Greek) king is named in Ashoka's Rock Edict II?
x: Rock Edict II names the Yavana king Antiyoka (Antiochus) and his neighbours, in whose lands Ashoka arranged medical care.

s: Which Major Rock Edict prohibited animal sacrifice and festive gatherings known as samaja?
x: Rock Edict I bans animal sacrifice and festive gatherings called samaja.

s: Which Major Rock Edict deals with medical care for men and animals and the planting of herbs and trees?
x: Major Rock Edict II discusses medical care for men and animals and the planting of herbs and trees. It also names the Chola, Chera, Pandya and Satyaputra kingdoms.

s: Which Major Rock Edict is correctly matched with its subject?
o: Rock Edict III – Dhammayatras replace pleasure tours
Rock Edict VIII – Quinquennial tours of officials
Rock Edict III – Pativedakas may report at all times
Rock Edict VI – Pativedakas may report at all times
x: RE VI deals with Pativedakas and the king being available at all times; RE III covers quinquennial tours and RE VIII Dhammayatras.

s: Which Major Rock Edict records the appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas?
x: RE V records the appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas, 13 years after consecration.

s: Five-yearly (quinquennial) tours of officials were ordered in which Major Rock Edict?
x: RE III orders quinquennial tours of officials.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ashoka freed prisoners on each anniversary of his coronation (Abhisheka).
2. Pillar Edict IV gave condemned prisoners a respite of three days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: prisoners were released on every coronation anniversary, and PE IV gave a 3-day respite to those sentenced to death.

s: Which of the following peoples is named in Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII among those following his Dhamma?
x: Rock Edict XIII lists the Andhras among the peoples following Dhamma; the other three came much later.

s: What is the subject of Ashoka's Major Rock Edict XII?
o: Medical care for men and animals
Religious tolerance and respect for all sects
x: RE XII asks for respect for all sects and restraint in speech about other faiths; medical care is RE II, Mahamattas RE V, Kalinga RE XIII.

s: Which southern kingdoms are named in Ashoka's Rock Edict II?
x: RE II names the Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputtas, Keralaputtas and Tamraparni (Sri Lanka) as neighbours.

s: Which Major Rock Edict of Ashoka says that Dhammayatras replaced the royal pleasure tours?
x: Rock Edict VIII records that Dhammayatras replaced pleasure tours; the first was to Bodh Gaya.

s: Most of Ashoka's inscriptions in India were written in which script?
x: Brahmi was used in most of India; Kharosthi was used in the north-west, Greek in Afghanistan and Aramaic at Kandahar and Laghman.

s:
Consider the following:
1. Brahmi was used only for writing Telugu.
2. Brahmi was the source of the Telugu script.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Brahmi is the source of the Telugu script, but it was not restricted to Telugu; most Ashokan edicts across the empire used it.

s: Which Ashokan edict site is correctly matched with its script or language?
x: Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna) is bilingual in Greek and Aramaic. Shahbazgarhi is in Kharosthi, Taxila in Aramaic and Girnar in Brahmi.

s: Which of the following is NOT named in any Ashokan edict?
x: No Ashokan edict names the Eightfold Path, the Four Noble Truths or Nibbana; even the Greek and Aramaic versions carry Buddhist ideas without naming the Buddha.

s: From which script is the Kharosthi script derived?
x: Kharosthi derives from the Aramaic script of the Achaemenid Persians.

s: Where were Ashokan edicts in the Aramaic script found?
x: Aramaic edicts come from Taxila, Laghman and Kandahar; Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are Kharosthi, Girnar Brahmi.

s: Where was the bilingual Greek-Aramaic edict of Ashoka found?
x: The Greek-Aramaic bilingual edict is at Kandahar (Shar-i-Kuna); Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra are Kharosthi sites.

s: Ashokan inscriptions are classified into which three groups?
x: Ashokan inscriptions are rock (major and minor rock edicts), pillar and cave (Barabar) inscriptions; copper-plates, seals and coin legends belong to later periods.

s: What is Pillar Edict II mainly concerned with?
x: Pillar Edict II defines Dhamma as 'few faults, many good deeds'. Appointing Dhamma Mahamatras is Rock Edict V, banning animal sacrifice is Rock Edict I, and the Kalinga War is recorded in Rock Edict XIII.

s: How were dissenting monks and nuns to be treated under the Schism Edict?
x: The Schism Edict orders that dissenting monks and nuns be expelled from the Sangha. It is found at Sarnath, Sanchi and Kaushambi.

s: Lumbini was granted which of the following concessions in the Rummindei pillar inscription?
o: Exemption from bhaga but increase of bali to one-eighth
Complete exemption from all royal taxes and military service
Exemption from bali and reduction of bhaga to one-eighth
Reduction of bali to one-half and bhaga to one-fourth
x: The village of Lumbini was exempted from bali, and its share of produce, bhaga, was reduced to one-eighth.

s: The Queen's edict recording the gifts of Karuvaki is found on which pillar?
x: The Queen's edict on Karuvaki's gifts is on the Allahabad-Kosam pillar, which later also received Samudragupta's prashasti.

s: Ashoka's Pillar Edict VII is found only on which pillar?
x: PE VII occurs only on the Delhi-Topra pillar; it says Dhamma spreads better by persuasion than by law.

s:
Consider the following about Ashoka's visit to Lumbini:
1. He visited Lumbini when he had been consecrated twenty years.
2. The visit is recorded in the Rummindei pillar inscription.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The Rummindei pillar records that Ashoka visited Lumbini after twenty years of his consecration; the eighth year refers to the Kalinga War.

s: Why are Ashokan pillar edicts concentrated in the Ganga plain?
o: River transport eased the movement of the heavy monoliths
Rock surfaces for edicts were absent there
Pillars were reserved for Buddhist monasteries
The pillars marked the route of the Kalinga campaign
x: The pillar edicts cluster in the Ganga plain because river transport made it easier to move the heavy monoliths.

s: Which Ashokan pillar later carried Samudragupta's prashasti?
x: The Allahabad-Kosam pillar, with PE I–VI and the Queen's edict, later bore Samudragupta's prashasti.

s: Who is traditionally said to have moved the Kosam (Kaushambi) pillar to the Allahabad fort?
x: Tradition credits Akbar with moving the Kosam pillar; Jahangir only added his inscription.

s: Which Pillar Edict gave Rajukas independent judicial power and a 3-day respite to condemned prisoners?
x: PE IV (26th year) gave Rajukas judicial power and a 3-day respite to the condemned.

s: Which two Ashokan pillars were brought to Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq?
x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq moved the Topra and Meerut pillars to Delhi; the Kosam pillar went to the Allahabad fort.

s: At which of the following places is Ashoka's Schism Edict found?
x: The Schism Edict, expelling dissenting monks and nuns, is found at Sarnath, Sanchi and Kaushambi.

s: Which Ashokan pillar inscription in Nepal records the enlargement of the Kanakamuni stupa?
x: The Nigali Sagar pillar in Nepal records that Ashoka enlarged the Kanakamuni stupa in his 14th year.

s: According to Ashoka's Pillar Edict VII, how does Dhamma spread best?
o: By persuasion rather than by law
By the conquest of neighbouring kingdoms
x: Pillar Edict VII (only on the Delhi-Topra pillar) says Dhamma spreads better by persuasion than by law.

s: Besides Ashoka's edicts and Samudragupta's prashasti, the inscription of which Mughal emperor is found on the Allahabad pillar?
x: Jahangir added his inscription to the Allahabad (Kosam) pillar, which had been moved to the Allahabad fort.

s: Which edicts of Ashoka are inscribed on the Lauriya Nandangarh pillar?
x: The Lauriya Nandangarh pillar bears Pillar Edicts I-VI in Brahmi script; PE VII is found only on the Delhi-Topra pillar.

s: In which district of Bihar is the Lauriya Nandangarh pillar of Ashoka?
x: The Lauriya Nandangarh pillar, with a single lion capital and Pillar Edicts I-VI, is in West Champaran district of Bihar.

s: Erragudi (Yerragudi), the Ashokan edict site, is now in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Kurnool); it is added as option 5.
No printed option is right: the Erragudi (Yerragudi/Jonnagiri) edicts are in Pattikonda mandal, which stayed in Kurnool district after the 2022 reorganisation – not Nandyal, Guntur, Anantapur or Prakasam. The printed key (Nandyal) is wrong.

s: In which language and script were the Ashokan inscriptions in Andhra Pradesh written?
x: The Andhra inscriptions of Ashoka were in Prakrit using the Brahmi script, and they show Mauryan administration extended into Rayalaseema.

s: Which are the two important Ashokan rock-edict sites in the Kurnool-Nandyal region?
x: Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri are the two important Ashokan rock-edict sites in the Kurnool-Nandyal region; Bhattiprolu is not an Ashokan edict site.

s: Which Ashokan inscription site is associated with evidence of the guru-disciple relationship?
x: Rajula Mandagiri (Kurnool, AP) is associated with the guru-disciple relationship. Kalsi has a set of Major Rock Edicts, Maski names Ashoka, and Kanaganahalli has the portrait label. (Erragudi records teachers instilling Dhamma in students.)

s: The Brahmagiri, Siddapura and Jatinga-Rameshwara Minor Rock Edicts are in which district of Karnataka?
x: These three Minor Rock Edict sites are in Chitradurga district; Maski is in Raichur, Gavimath in Koppal.

s: Which Ashokan edict asks teachers to instil Dhamma in their students?
x: The Erragudi Minor Rock Edict (now Nandyal district, AP) says teachers should instil Dhamma in their students.

s: What is the main subject of the Erragudi Minor Rock Edict of Ashoka?
o: The personal name of Ashoka as Buddhashakya
Duty of teachers to instil Dhamma in students
x: Erragudi asks teachers to instil Dhamma in students; the name Buddhashakya is at Maski and the Lumbini exemption at Rummindei.

s: Why are the Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri edicts important for the history of Andhra?
o: They are the earliest inscriptions found in Andhra
They are the only Ashokan edicts in Kharosthi
They give the personal name of Ashoka
They describe the Kalinga War in detail
x: These Prakrit-Brahmi edicts are the earliest inscriptions in Andhra and show that Mauryan rule reached Rayalaseema.

s: Which edict of Ashoka recommends Buddhist texts and proves that he was a Buddhist?
x: In the Bhabru (Bairat) edict Ashoka states his faith in the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha and recommends Buddhist texts.

s: In which district of Karnataka is the Maski Minor Rock Edict of Ashoka?
x: Maski, the Minor Rock Edict that names Ashoka, is in Raichur district of Karnataka.

s: Which source is associated with the reference to Kashmir through Ashoka’s son Jalauka?
x: Rajatarangini refers to Kashmir in connection with Ashoka’s son Jalauka.

s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Site — Present location
x: Girnar is located at Junagadh in Gujarat. Kalsi is in Uttarakhand, while Dhauli and Jaugada are in Odisha.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Maski — Minor Rock Edict naming Ashoka
Rummindei — Major Rock Edict site in Nepal
x: Rummindei is a pillar inscription site at Lumbini in Nepal, not a Major Rock Edict site. Sopara, Rajula Mandagiri and Maski are correctly matched.

s: What is the main evidence for determining the extent of Ashoka's empire?
x: The geographical spread of Ashokan edict sites is the principal evidence for the extent of his empire.

s: Near which place are the Kalsi Rock Edicts of Ashoka located?
x: The Kalsi rock edicts of Ashoka are near Dehradun in Uttarakhand.

s:
Consider the following:
1. Dhauli is associated with Ashokan rock edicts and Kalinga.
2. Jaugada is associated with Ashokan rock edicts and Odisha.
3. Besnagar is associated with the Heliodorus Pillar and the Bhagavata religion.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Dhauli and Jaugada in Odisha carry Ashoka's Kalinga rock edicts, and Besnagar (Vidisha) has the Heliodorus (Garuda) Pillar linked to the Bhagavata religion.

s: At which one of the following places has a Major Rock Edict of Ashoka been found?
x: Girnar near Junagadh in Gujarat carries the 14 Major Rock Edicts. Barabar has cave inscriptions, while Allahabad and Delhi-Topra are pillar edict sites.

s: Which of the following is NOT an Ashokan edict site?
x: Besnagar (Vidisha) has the Heliodorus (Garuda) Pillar of the Bhagavata religion, not an Ashokan edict.

s: In which present-day state is Sopara, a Major Rock Edict site of Ashoka?
x: Sopara is in Palghar/Thane, Maharashtra.

s: In which state is the Ashokan edict site of Erragudi located?
x: Erragudi (Yerragudi), with Major and Minor Rock Edicts, is in Andhra Pradesh. It is now in Nandyal district, earlier part of Kurnool district.

s: The Girnar rock, which bears Ashoka's 14 Major Rock Edicts, also carries the inscription of which later ruler?
x: The same rock at Girnar (Junagadh, Gujarat) that bears Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts later received Rudradaman's inscription.

s: In which district of Gujarat is Girnar, the site of Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts?
x: Girnar, with all 14 Major Rock Edicts, is in Junagadh district of Gujarat.

s: In which district of Odisha is the Ashokan edict site of Jaugada?
x: Jaugada, with Major Rock Edicts and the Separate Kalinga Edicts, is in Ganjam district of Odisha.

s: The Separate Kalinga Edicts at Dhauli and Jaugada replaced which Major Rock Edicts in those regions?
x: At Dhauli and Jaugada, the Separate Kalinga Edicts replace Major Rock Edicts XI–XIII and address officers of Tosali and Samapa.

s: To the officers of which places were Ashoka's Separate Kalinga Edicts addressed?
x: The Separate Kalinga Edicts address officers of Tosali and Samapa, telling them to stop unjust imprisonment and torture.

s: In which edicts does Ashoka declare 'All men are my children'?
x: The Separate Kalinga Edicts at Dhauli and Jaugada, addressed to the officers of Tosali and Samapa, say 'all men are my children'.

s: Where are Ashoka's Separate Kalinga Edicts found?
x: The Separate Kalinga Edicts are at Dhauli and Jaugada in Odisha, where they replace Rock Edicts XI-XIII.

s: Who was the Vyavaharika among Kautilya's tirthas?
x: Vyavaharika was the civil judge; Prashasta looked after prisons, Nayaka was the city guard and Paura the capital's governor.

s: The Sannidhata in the Mauryan administration was primarily responsible for which of the following?
x: Sannidhata was the treasurer and keeper of state stores. The Samaharta, in contrast, was the Collector-General of Revenue.

s: Which dynasties of Andhra later adopted the Mauryan model of the Saptanga state and the 18 Tirthas?
x: The Eastern Chalukyas (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and the Kakatiyas used the Saptanga and 18 Tirthas model. The Sungas, Kanvas, Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Kushanas and Western Kshatrapas are not linked with it.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Pradeshtri — Criminal justice and kantakashodhana courts
x: Pradeshtri was associated with criminal justice and presided over kantakashodhana courts. Dauvarika guarded the palace gate, Antapala guarded the frontier, and Karmantika dealt with factories and mines.

s: Among Kautilya's tirthas, what was the Antapala in charge of?
x: The Antapala was the frontier officer in charge of border forts.

s: Which Mauryan tirtha was in charge of prisons?
x: The Prashasta handled prisons; Dauvarika the palace gate, Nayaka the city guard and Paura the capital.

s: What was the main duty of the Samaharta in the Mauryan administration?
o: Keeping the treasury and state stores
x: The Samaharta was the collector-general of revenue; the Sannidhata kept the treasury.

s: Which of Kautilya's eighteen tirthas was the head of the army department?
x: The Dandapala headed the army department; Samaharta collected revenue, Sannidhata was treasurer, Antapala guarded the frontier.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Tirtha) - List-II (Department)
A. Samaharta - 1. Frontier forts
B. Sannidhata - 2. Army
C. Dandapala - 3. Treasury and state stores
D. Antapala - 4. Collection of revenue
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Samaharta collected revenue, Sannidhata kept the treasury, Dandapala headed the army and Antapala guarded the frontier.

s: Among Kautilya's tirthas, what was the Karmantika in charge of?
x: The Karmantika was the tirtha in charge of factories and mines.

s: In the Mauryan administration, what was the Akaradhyaksha in charge of?
x: Akaradhyaksha supervised mines; Panyadhyaksha handled commerce, Koshadhyaksha the treasury and Lavanadhyaksha salt.

s: With which department was the Mauryan Lakshanadhyaksha associated?
x: Lakshanadhyaksha was associated with the mint and seals; forest produce was under the Kupyadhyaksha and storehouses under the Koshthagaradhyaksha.

s: What was the Mauryan Sulkadhyaksha in charge of?
x: The Sulkadhyaksha collected tolls and trade and service taxes.

s: Which Mauryan superintendent was in charge of crown-land agriculture?
x: The Sitadhyaksha supervised crown-land farming and collected sita.

s: What did the Panyadhyaksha supervise in the Mauryan administration?
x: The Panyadhyaksha handled commerce; the Sulkadhyaksha took tolls and the Lavanadhyaksha handled salt.

s: Who was the Akshapataladhyaksha in the Mauryan administration?
x: The Akshapataladhyaksha was the accountant-general in charge of currency and accounts offices.

s: Which pair of Mauryan superintendent and charge is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The Kupyadhyaksha handled forest produce; mines were under the Akaradhyaksha.

s: What did the Pautavadhyaksha deal with in the Mauryan administration?
x: Pautavadhyaksha handled weights and measures; Sitadhyaksha looked after crown lands and Panyadhyaksha state trade.

s: What was the fine for slushing the road with dirt and water called in the Arthashastra?
x: Pankodakasannirodhe was the civic fine for slushing the road; Pranaya, Pindakara and Vivita were revenue terms.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Pindakara — Tax assessed on groups of villages
Pranaya — Tax paid only in cash
x: Pindakara was a tax assessed collectively on groups of villages. Bhaga was the king’s share of produce, Pranaya an emergency tax and Hiranya a cash tax.

s:
Consider the following about Bhaga in the Mauryan revenue system:
1. It was an emergency levy imposed during war.
2. It was normally the king's one-sixth share of the produce.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Bhaga was the king's share of agricultural produce, generally one-sixth (Megasthenes gives one-fourth to one-sixth); the emergency levy was Pranaya.

s:
According to Megasthenes:
1. The king was regarded as owner of all land.
2. Land revenue was collected directly by royal officials.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Megasthenes stated that the king owned all land and that royal officials collected the revenue directly.

s: Which Mauryan tax was paid only in cash?
x: Hiranya was a cash-only tax; Pranaya was the emergency tax.

s: From what were Vivita dues collected in the Mauryan revenue system?
x: Vivita was pasture land dues; sita came from crown land.

s: According to Megasthenes, what was the penalty for evading sales tax?
x: Megasthenes records death as the penalty for evading sales tax.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mauryan revenue system:
1. Pranaya was an emergency tax.
2. Bhaga was normally one-sixth of the produce.
3. Bali was the income from crown land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; income from crown land was sita, while bali was an additional levy.

s: Which Mauryan revenue term is correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Sita – Pasture land and its dues
x: Pranaya was the emergency tax or 'gift of affection'; Sita was income from crown land and Vivita pasture land and its dues.

s: In the Mauryan revenue system, on what was Pindakara levied?
x: Pindakara was levied on groups of villages; vivita was pasture dues, vana forests and setu gardens.

s: Which of the following Mauryan officials worked at the village level rather than the district level?
x: The Gramika was the village head, whereas Rajukas, Pradeshikas and Yuktas were district-level officials.

s: Which Mauryan officials handled land survey and assessment and also possessed judicial powers?
x: Rajukas handled land survey and assessment and had judicial powers, while Yuktas were subordinate revenue or secretarial officers.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Astynomoi — City administration through six municipal boards
Agronomoi — Roads, irrigation and land measurement
x: Rakshinas were the city police. Frontier forts were guarded by Anta-mahamattas; Agronomoi, Astynomoi and Dhamma Mahamattas have been correctly matched.

s: Which Mauryan official acted as accountant over 5-10 villages?
x: The Gopa was the accountant over 5-10 villages; the Sthanika collected taxes over a larger division and the Gramika was the village head.

s: Mahabaladhikrita, Mahadandanayaka and Mahasandhivigrahika were official titles of which dynasty?
x: These were Gupta titles, not Mauryan officials such as Panyadhyaksha, Samaharta, Rajuka or Gopa.

s: Who was the Sthanika in Mauryan local administration?
o: Tax collector over a larger division
x: The Sthanika collected taxes over a larger division; the Gramika was village head and the Gopa an accountant.

s: Who headed the municipal administration of a Mauryan city?
x: A Mauryan city was run by a municipality under the Nagaraka (Purmukhya).

s: Who was the chief district administrator in the Mauryan empire, in charge of revenue and police?
x: The Pradeshika was the chief district administrator, handling revenue and police and touring every five years (RE III).

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Manufactured goods committee — Inspection of manufactured goods
Committee for foreigners — Foreign residents and visitors
Commerce committee — Trade, prices, weights and measures
Sales-tax committee — Collection of land revenue
x: The sixth committee dealt with tax on sales, including imports and exports; it did not collect land revenue.

s: What were Megasthenes' Agronomoi in charge of?
o: Districts – roads, irrigation and land measurement
x: Agronomoi were district officers; Astynomoi were the city officers.

s: How many members made up Megasthenes' municipal board of Pataliputra?
x: Pataliputra had 30 members in 6 committees of 5 each.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan army administration according to Megasthenes:
1. It was run by six boards of five members each.
2. The navy was one of its boards.
3. Chandragupta's army had 30,000 cavalry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: six boards of five, including the navy, and an army of 6,00,000 foot and 30,000 cavalry.

s: What did the sixth municipal committee of Pataliputra described by Megasthenes deal with?
x: The sixth committee collected a one-tenth tax on sales, not land revenue.

s: According to Megasthenes, how many foot soldiers did Chandragupta Maurya's army have?
x: Megasthenes gives Chandragupta's army as 6,00,000 foot soldiers and 30,000 cavalry.

s: Which council of ministers acted as a check on the authority of the Mauryan king?
x: The Mantriparishad, along with paura-janapada assemblies and public opinion, checked the king's authority - a chariot cannot move on one wheel.

s: How is the highly centralised Mauryan government, with the king heading executive, legislature and judiciary, described?
x: Mauryan government was highly centralised under the king and has been described as paternal despotism.

s: Kautilya's saying 'a chariot cannot move on one wheel' stresses the king's need for what?
x: Kautilya meant that the king cannot rule alone and needs ministers (the Mantriparishad), a check on his power.

s: In Kautilya's Saptanga theory, which element comes first in the standard order?
x: The standard order is Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda/Bala and Mitra, so Swami comes first.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven standard elements in Kautilya's Saptanga theory?
x: The standard seven elements do not include Shatru; some lists add it only as an eighth item.

s: In Kautilya's Saptanga theory, which element is called 'the ear of the state'?
x: Mitra (ally), the seventh limb, is called the ear of the state.

s: Which element comes third in Kautilya's Saptanga order?
x: The order is Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda and Mitra.

s: What was the capital of the Mauryan province of Dakshinapatha?
x: Suvarnagiri was the capital of Dakshinapatha; Pataliputra, Taxila and Ujjain were the capitals of Magadha, Uttarapatha and Avantirashtra.

s: What were districts called in Mauryan provincial administration?
x: Mauryan districts were called Vish or Ahara; Chandragupta's four provinces were ruled by Kumaras or governors.

s: The province of Kalinga, added to the Mauryan Empire by Ashoka, had which capital?
x: Tosali was the provincial capital of Kalinga after its incorporation under Ashoka.

s: Which was the largest settlement unit in the Arthashastra, consisting of 800 villages?
x: Sthaniya had 800 villages; Dronamukha had 400, Kharvatika 200 and Sangrahana 10.

s: What were the princes who mainly governed the Mauryan provinces called?
x: Provinces were ruled by Kumaras (princes) or governors, helped by Mahamatras.

s: Ujjain was the capital of which Mauryan province?
x: Ujjain was the capital of Avantipatha; Taxila, Suvarnagiri and Tosali were the others.

s: What was Suvarnagiri in the Mauryan administration?
o: The southern capital of the empire
The northern capital of the empire
The principal centre of the Paura-janapada
x: Suvarnagiri was the southern capital of the Mauryan Empire. It was associated with the Dakshinapatha and the administration of the Deccan.

s: Which is the correct order of the settlement units in the Arthashastra, from the largest to the smallest?
x: Sthaniya had 800 villages, Dronamukha 400, Kharvatika 200 and Sangrahana 10.

s: Which was the capital of the Mauryan province of Uttarapatha?
x: Taxila was the capital of Uttarapatha; Ujjain of Avantipatha, Suvarnagiri of Dakshinapatha and Tosali of Kalinga.

s: How many provinces did the Mauryan empire have under Chandragupta Maurya?
x: There were four provinces under Chandragupta; Kalinga (Tosali) was added later by Ashoka.

s: What were the spies who watched officials and provinces called in the Mauryan system?
x: Gudhapurushas were spies who watched officials and provinces; Samstha spies were stationary and Sanchara spies wandering.

s: What were stationary spies called in the Mauryan espionage system?
x: Samstha spies were stationary; Sanchara spies, such as tikshna and rasada, were wandering.

s: Which of the following was a wandering (sanchara) spy in the Mauryan system?
x: Parivrajika (women) were wandering spies; kapatika, grihapatika and vaidehaka were stationary (samstha).

s: Which of the following did Megasthenes state about Mauryan law?
o: A fully codified penal code existed
Punishment was the same for all varnas
x: Megasthenes stated that there was no written code; Mauryan punishments included fines, mutilation and death, and their severity varied by varna.

s: With which system of the Mauryan administration is the term 'Pradvivaka' associated?
x: Pradvivaka was the chief judicial adviser or judge (APPSC G2 2019: judicial system). Revenue was under the Samaharta, espionage under the gudhapurushas, and the municipal boards were the Astynomoi of Megasthenes.

s: In the Mauryan judicial hierarchy, which court stood just above the village court?
x: The judicial ladder ran from the village court to Sangrahana, Dronamukha, Janapada and finally the king.

s: What were the Mauryan courts that tried civil cases such as marriage, contract and inheritance called?
x: Dharmasthiya courts were civil courts, whereas Kantakashodhana ('removal of thorns') courts were criminal courts.

s: Who presided over the Mauryan kantakashodhana courts?
x: Kantakashodhana (criminal) courts had three pradeshtris; dharmasthiya (civil) courts had three dharmasthas.

s: Which Mauryan courts, meaning 'removal of thorns', tried criminal cases?
x: Kantakashodhana courts tried criminal cases under three pradeshtris; Dharmasthiya courts tried civil cases.

s: With whose remains is Stupa No. 3 at Sanchi associated?
o: Monks of the Ashokan missionary era
x: Stupa No. 3 at Sanchi holds relics of the Buddha's disciples Sariputra (Sariputta) and Mudgalayana (Moggallana).

s: According to tradition, Ashoka redistributed the Buddha's relics from eight stupas into how many stupas?
x: Tradition states that Ashoka redistributed the relics from the original eight stupas into 84,000 stupas.

s: Which stupa is correctly matched with its location?
o: Amaravati Stupa – Right bank of the Krishna, Andhra Pradesh
x: Amaravati is on the right bank of the Krishna; Sanchi is in Raisen, Bharhut in Satna and Dhamek at Sarnath.

s: Who built the Ranabhar (Ramabhar) Stupa at Kushinagar over the Buddha's cremation site?
x: Ranabhar Stupa was built by the Mallas, unlike Sanchi, the original Dhamek Stupa and the Kanakamuni Stupa, which are associated with Ashoka.

s: Which stupa was traced by Colin Mackenzie in 1797?
x: Amaravati was traced by Mackenzie in 1797; Bharhut was discovered by Cunningham, Sanchi is rated finest architecturally and Dhamek's present form is Gupta.

s: Where is the Kanakamuni Stupa located?
x: Kanakamuni Stupa is at Niglihawa in Nepal; Ranabhar is at Kushinagar and Dhamek at Sarnath.

s: Who discovered the Bharhut stupa?
x: Bharhut, a Sunga stupa of c. 150 BC, was found by Cunningham.

s: The present form of the Dhamek stupa at Sarnath belongs to which period?
x: The Dhamek stupa had an Ashokan original, but its present form is Gupta.

s: Which is the oldest stupa of Andhra?
x: Bhattiprolu is Andhra's oldest stupa.

s: At which places are the Dharmarajika stupas found?
x: The Dharmarajika stupas are at Sarnath and Taxila.

s: In which district of Madhya Pradesh is the Sanchi stupa?
x: Sanchi (Kaknam) is in Raisen district, MP, west of the Betwa; Bharhut is in Satna.

s: Which one of the following is the oldest stone structure in India?
x: The Sanchi Stupa, begun under Ashoka, is the oldest of the four. Ajanta's caves are later (mostly Satavahana to Vakataka), Brihadeeswara is Chola (11th c.) and Konark is 13th-century.

s: Megasthenes reported that which of the following did NOT exist in India?
x: Megasthenes stated that India had no slavery, while describing hereditary occupations and endogamy.

s: According to the Arthashastra, how could a person become a slave?
o: Birth, sale, capture in war and judicial punishment
x: The Arthashastra recognised slavery arising through birth, sale, capture in war and judicial punishment.

s: What was the divorce that a wife deserted by her husband could seek called in the Arthashastra?
x: The Arthashastra recognised moksha for a deserted wife; anuloma and pratiloma refer to types of inter-varna marriage.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Karmakaras were hired wage labourers. Vishti meant unpaid forced labour for the state, while shreni referred to a guild.

s: Which untouchable groups grew in number during the Mauryan period?
x: Chandalas and Shvapakas, untouchable groups, grew in number in the Mauryan period.

s: What did Stridhana refer to in the Arthashastra?
o: Property belonging exclusively to the king
A woman's own property, including jewellery and maintenance
Land held jointly by a village community
x: Stridhana was a woman's own property, including jewellery and resources for maintenance.

s: What were the five mixed castes outside Aryan society called in the Arthashastra?
x: Kautilya referred to five mixed castes called Antyavasayins as outside Aryan society; learned men were called Sishtas.

s: Which was the most famous centre of learning during the Mauryan period?
x: Taxila was the most famous Mauryan-period centre of learning, ahead of Ujjain and Varanasi.

s: Which one of the following statements about female slaves is NOT correct?
o: Freedom could be obtained by payment.
A female slave who bore her master a son became free.
A penalty existed for selling a pregnant slave without arranging maternity protection.
The son of a female slave was denied any legal connection with the master.
x: The son of a female slave who bore her master a child was entitled to the legal status of the master's son. The other statements reflect protections or routes to freedom.

s: How many categories of slaves (dasas) does Kautilya list in the Arthashastra?
x: Kautilya lists nine categories of slaves; seven is the number of Megasthenes' social classes.

s: Whose envoy was Megasthenes at Chandragupta's court?
x: Megasthenes was the Greek envoy of Seleucus and wrote the Indica.

s: What was unpaid forced labour called in the Arthashastra?
x: Vishti was unpaid forced labour (Telugu Vetti); karmakara was wage labour.

s: According to the Arthashastra, which of the following could NOT be made a slave?
o: A person punished by a court
x: Slaves came through birth, sale, war capture or judicial punishment, but no Arya could be made a slave.

s: What were learned men called in Mauryan society?
x: Sishtas were learned men; Antyavasayins were the five mixed castes outside Aryan society.

s: What does the term 'Moksha' mean in the Arthashastra?
x: Moksha meant divorce; stridhana was a woman's property and vishti forced labour.

s: Into how many classes did Megasthenes divide Indian society in his Indica?
x: Megasthenes listed seven classes, from philosophers and farmers to councillors and assessors.

s: Who is the author of Indica?
x: Megasthenes, the Greek envoy of Seleucus at Chandragupta's court, wrote Indica in Greek.

s: With which work is Kautilya's Arthashastra often compared?
x: The Arthashastra, on polity and wealth, is compared with Machiavelli's The Prince.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mauryan society:
1. The Arthashastra allowed widow remarriage.
2. Shudras could own land.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Widow remarriage was allowed in the Arthashastra, and Shudras could own land.

s: Which two types of philosophers did Megasthenes describe in India?
x: Megasthenes divided philosophers into Brahmins and Shramanas.

s: Yaksha worship was shared by which religious traditions?
x: Yakshas were revered in Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism alike.

s: Mauryan yaksha-yakshi statues and terracotta figurines belong to which category of art?
x: Yaksha-yakshi statues and terracotta figurines are folk art; palaces, pillars, stupas and caves are royal art.

s: Where was the nude male torso of early Indian art found?
x: The nude male torso comes from Lohanipur, Patna; Kumrahar has the 80-pillared hall and Rampurva the bull capital.

s: The polished chauri-bearer Didarganj Yakshi belongs to which period?
x: The Didarganj Yakshi is a Mauryan work, like the Dhauli elephant, Ashoka's brick stupa at Sanchi and the Kumrahar hall.

s: Which pair of folk sculpture and findspot is correctly matched?
x: A Yakshi comes from Besnagar; the chauri-bearer is from Didarganj, Manibhadra from Parkham and the nude torso from Lohanipur.

s: The Mauryan rock-cut elephant at Dhauli is near which river?
x: The Dhauli elephant stands by the Daya river near Bhubaneswar.

s: Which of the following is NOT a Mauryan work of art?
x: The Kanaganahalli slab is Satavahana-era; Dhauli, Didarganj and Kumrahar are all Mauryan.

s: Which pair is correctly matched in relation to popular art of the Mauryan period?
x: The inscribed Manibhadra Yaksha was found at Parkham near Mathura. The chauri-bearer Yakshi is from Didarganj near Patna (a Yakshi, not a Yaksha), Besnagar is associated with a Yakshi, and Noh with a Yaksha.

s: Among the following, which is the correct chronological order from earliest to latest?
o: Dhauli elephant — Udayagiri Varaha — Mahabalipuram monuments — Lingaraja Temple
Udayagiri Varaha — Dhauli elephant — Lingaraja Temple — Mahabalipuram monuments
Dhauli elephant — Mahabalipuram monuments — Udayagiri Varaha — Lingaraja Temple
Lingaraja Temple — Dhauli elephant — Udayagiri Varaha — Mahabalipuram monuments
x: The Dhauli elephant belongs to the third century BCE and is earlier than the Gupta Udayagiri Varaha, Pallava monuments at Mahabalipuram and the Lingaraja Temple.

s: What was Sita land in the Mauryan economy?
o: Forest land reserved exclusively for hunting
Land donated permanently to Buddhist monasteries
Land owned collectively by village artisans
Crown land cultivated directly under state supervision
x: Sita was crown land cultivated for the state, under the supervision of the Sitadhyaksha, often using slaves and hired labourers.

s: How were mining, forestry, salt, liquor, arms and metallurgy run in the Mauryan period?
x: The Mauryan state exercised monopoly or strong control over mining, forestry, salt, liquor, arms and metallurgy.

s: Which pottery was typical of the Mauryan period?
x: NBPW was the typical Mauryan pottery.

s: Who cultivated Sita (crown) land in the Mauryan period?
x: Sita land was farmed for the state using slaves and hired labourers, not exclusively by free peasants.

s: What annual rate of interest is mentioned in the Arthashastra?
x: The Arthashastra mentions an annual interest rate of 15 percent.

s: In which unit was rainfall measured near granaries in the Mauryan period?
x: Rainfall was measured in drona; pana, mashaka and kakani were coins.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mauryan economy?
o: Good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts
Shrenis financed early Buddhist centres, including in Andhra
The state took a road tax from trade caravans
Mauryan coins bore portraits of the emperor
x: Mauryan punch-marked silver coins carried symbols but no portraits; the other three statements are correct.

s:
Consider the following about Mauryan imperial currency:
1. It consisted mainly of punch-marked silver coins.
2. The coins bore portraits of the emperors.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Mauryan currency was mainly punch-marked silver coins carrying symbols such as peacocks and hills, not portraits.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Suvarna was a gold coin. Mashaka and Kakani were copper, while Pana or karshapana was silver.

s: What was the value of the Mauryan copper coin Kakani?
x: The Kakani was a copper coin worth 1/4 mashaka.

s: Which pair of Mauryan coin and metal is correctly matched?
x: Mashaka and kakani were copper, pana silver and suvarna gold.

s: Who among the following funded early Buddhist centres, including those in Andhra, in the Mauryan period?
x: Guilds (shrenis), merchants and artisans gave money to early Buddhist centres, including those in Andhra.

s: To which age do the punch-marked silver coins of India go back?
x: Punch-marked silver coins, with symbols and no portraits, go back to the Mahajanapada age (6th c. BCE).

s: Who led trade caravans in the Mauryan period?
x: Caravans were led by a Sarthavaha, and the state collected road tax in return for protecting them.

s: The Uttarapatha connected which of the following routes?
o: Rajgir through Kalinga to Sri Lanka
x: Uttarapatha was the northern highway running from Taxila through Pataliputra to Tamralipti.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tamralipti – Principal port of the Ganga basin
x: Tamralipti was an east-coast port, the principal port of the Ganga basin; Sopara and Bharukachchha were west-coast ports.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Mauryan trade routes?
o: Dakshinapatha was the great southern trade route
Dakshinapatha was the northern highway from Taxila to Tamralipti
The Krishna–Godavari delta was a node of Dakshinapatha
Uttarapatha ran from Taxila through Pataliputra to Tamralipti
x: The Taxila–Tamralipti highway was Uttarapatha; Dakshinapatha was the southern route with the Krishna–Godavari delta as a node.

s: Which Red Sea port was associated with Mauryan trade with Egypt?
x: The Egyptian connection through the Red Sea was linked with the port of Bernis, or Berenice.

s: Which of the following were among the exports of the Mauryan period?
x: Diamonds, pearls, muslin and fine textiles were among the exports of the period.

s: Where was the Mauryan port of Bharukachchha (Broach) located?
x: Bharukachchha and Sopara were west-coast ports; Berenice was on the Red Sea.

s: Which of the following is true of Mauryan pillars?
o: Fluted wooden shafts with bronze capitals
Multi-block granite pillars with square bases
Monolithic circular shafts of Chunar sandstone with a lustrous polish
Composite brick pillars covered with lime plaster
x: Mauryan pillars were monolithic, free-standing and circular, generally made of Chunar sandstone and finished with the characteristic Mauryan polish.

s: In a Mauryan pillar, which component sits directly on top of the shaft?
x: The order is shaft, bell-shaped inverted lotus, abacus and animal capital; Mauryan pillars have no base.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the debate on Persian influence on Mauryan pillars?
o: Both traditions show polished surfaces and animal capitals
Mauryan pillars generally have bases like Persian pillars
Mauryan edicts resemble those of Darius in form and some expressions
Mauryan shafts are smooth, while Persian shafts are generally fluted
x: Mauryan pillars generally lack the bases characteristic of Persian pillars; the other three statements are correct.

s: Where was the Mauryan bull capital found?
x: The bull capital is from Rampurva; Sankisa has the elephant, Lauriya Nandangarh the single lion and Sarnath the four lions.

s: Of which stone were the shafts of Mauryan pillars made?
x: Mauryan pillars are monolithic shafts of Chunar sandstone with the Mauryan polish.

s: Which feature of Mauryan pillars marks them out from Achaemenid (Persian) pillars?
x: Polish, animal capitals and the 'lipi' idiom are Achaemenid similarities; the absence of a base is a Mauryan difference.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Pillar capital) - List-II (Site)
A. Four lions - 1. Sankisa
B. Bull - 2. Lauriya Nandangarh
C. Single lion - 3. Rampurva
D. Elephant - 4. Sarnath
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Four lions are at Sarnath, the bull at Rampurva, the single lion at Lauriya Nandangarh and the elephant at Sankisa.

s: What is the Sarnath capital known as in modern India?
x: The Sarnath capital has been adopted as the National Emblem of India.

s: By what name are the seven caves of the Barabar-Nagarjuni group collectively known?
x: The seven caves together are called Satghar, meaning ‘Seven Houses’.

s: The Lomas Rishi cave belongs to which group of caves?
x: Lomas Rishi and Karna Chopar belong to Barabar, while Gopika and Vadathika are Nagarjuni caves.

s: The dedicatory Brahmi inscriptions in the Barabar caves refer to Ashoka by which title?
x: The dedicatory Brahmi inscriptions refer to Ashoka as ‘King Piyadasi’.

s: The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves are located in which district of Bihar?
x: The caves are in Jehanabad district, near Gaya, and their dedicatory inscriptions are Mauryan, of the 3rd century BCE.

s: Which feature of the Lomas Rishi cave is regarded as an early example in Indian rock-cut architecture?
o: A stone ogee-shaped arch at the entrance
x: The Lomas Rishi entrance has the earliest known stone ogee, or horseshoe-shaped, arch. It imitates the form of a thatched wooden hut.

s: Which of the following are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India?
x: The Barabar caves in Bihar, dedicated by Ashoka to the Ajivikas in the 3rd century BCE, are India's oldest surviving rock-cut caves. Badami, Ajanta and Ellora are all later.

s: Which is the largest cave of the Nagarjuni group?
x: Gopika is the largest of the three Nagarjuni caves; Lomas Rishi is in the Barabar hills.

s: Into which rock are the Barabar caves cut?
x: The Barabar caves are cut into granite with a mirror polish.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Nagarjuni caves:
1. They are in Bihar.
2. Their inscriptions belong to the 6th century CE.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Nagarjuni caves are in Jehanabad, Bihar; their inscriptions are 3rd century BCE, not 6th century.

s: To which sect did Ashoka and Dasaratha give the Barabar and Nagarjuni caves?
x: The Barabar and Nagarjuni caves were given to the Ajivikas, not to Buddhists.

s: Which Mauryan rulers gave the Barabar and Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas?
x: Ashoka gave the Barabar caves and his grandson Dasaratha the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas.

s: Which of the following caves is on the Barabar hill?
x: The Barabar hill has four caves: Lomas Rishi, Sudama, Viswamitra and Karna Chopar; Gopika, Vahiyaka and Vadathika are Nagarjuni caves.

s: With the palaces of which cities did Megasthenes compare Chandragupta's palace at Pataliputra?
x: Megasthenes compared the palace to Susa and Ecbatana; Fa-Hien admired it in the 5th century CE.

s:
Assertion (A): Mauryan Pataliputra was mainly a wooden city, with a wooden wall having towers and gates.
Reason (R): Its excavated remains show that the entire city was built exclusively of stone.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is true: timber was the principal material, though polished stone pillars were used in important structures. R is false: the city was not built exclusively of stone.

s: Which archaeological site yielded remains of the wooden palisade of Pataliputra?
x: Bulandibagh yielded remains of the wooden palisade associated with the city of Pataliputra.

s: Where was the 80-pillared hall of Mauryan Pataliputra found?
x: Kumrahar yielded the 80-pillared hall; Bulandibagh yielded the wooden palisade.

s: Who excavated the Mauryan remains of Pataliputra?
x: D.B. Spooner excavated Mauryan Pataliputra.

s: Which Chinese pilgrim of the 5th century CE admired the Mauryan palace at Pataliputra?
x: Fa-Hien (5th c. CE) admired the palace at Pataliputra; Megasthenes compared it to Susa and Ecbatana.

s: What was the broad religious policy of the Mauryan state?
o: Complete separation of religion from the state
Liberal and tolerant, while protecting varna and ashrama
x: Mauryan religious conditions were liberal and tolerant, allowing freedom of faith, while the state protected varna and ashrama.

s: By which epithet was Kautilya, a Brahmana of the Mauryan period, described?
x: Brahmanism continued under the Mauryas, and Kautilya was a Brahmana called 'dvijarshabh'.

s: Which Mauryan ruler followed Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola?
x: Chandragupta, a follower of Jainism, went with Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola.

s: Which Ashokan edict names the Ajivikas and Nirgranthas separately?
x: PE VII names the Ajivikas and Nirgranthas (Jainas) separately.

s: Balirajgarh fort, excavated by the ASI and yielding punch-marked coins, is in which district of Bihar?
x: Balirajgarh is in Madhubani district, Bihar; its habitation runs from the Mauryan to the Pala period.

s: What may the site of Vaishya Tekri at Ujjain contain?
o: A third-century BCE stupa larger than Sanchi, along with punch-marked and cast Avanti coins
The earliest known Iron Age settlement of South India
A Kushana palace containing only gold coins
A Gupta-period university at the Uttarapatha junction
x: Vaishya Tekri may contain a third-century BCE stupa larger than Sanchi and has yielded punch-marked and cast Avanti coins. Excavation is expected to resume after about 90 years.

s: Whose reign does the Hathigumpha inscription record year by year?
x: The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri, near Bhubaneswar, records Kharavela's reign year by year; it belongs to the 2nd century BC.

s:
Consider the following statements about Kharavela:
1. He raided Magadha and brought back the Jina image taken by the Nandas.
2. He sent an army west only after an alliance with Satakarni.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: Kharavela raided Magadha and recovered the Jina image the Nandas had taken. Statement 2 is wrong: he sent an army west ignoring Satakarni, not in alliance with him. So '1 only'.

s: Which one of the following pairs of ruler and inscription is correctly matched?
x: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription is at Udayagiri near Bhubaneswar. The Nanaghat inscription belongs to the Satavahana queen Naganika, so pairing it with Rudradaman or Kharavela is wrong, and Naganika has nothing to do with Hathigumpha.

s: Kharavela of Kalinga belonged to which line?
x: Kharavela, a Jaina ruler, belonged to the Chedi (Mahameghavahana) line.

s: Which river is called Kannabenna in the Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela?
x: The Hathigumpha inscription calls the Krishna river Kannabenna (Kanhabenna).

s: According to the Hathigumpha inscription, which ruler did Kharavela ignore when he sent an army to the west?
x: Kharavela sent his army west ignoring the Satavahana king Satakarni.

s: Who among the following post-Mauryan kings was a follower of Jainism?
x: Kharavela of Kalinga was a Jaina; he brought back the Jina image taken by the Nandas.

s: Brihadratha, the last Mauryan king, was which king after Ashoka?
x: Brihadratha was the 7th king after Ashoka.

s: What do the Puranas call the Satavahanas?
x: The Satavahanas, earlier Mauryan feudatories, are called Andhra-bhrityas in the Puranas.

s: Under whom did the Andhra or Deccan region break away from Mauryan control?
o: Satavahanas, who had earlier been Mauryan feudatories
x: The Satavahanas, earlier Mauryan feudatories, emerged as the breakaway power in the Andhra or Deccan region.

s:
Consider the following about the Pushyamitra Sunga persecution debate:
1. The Divyavadana describes Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists.
2. Sanchi and Bharhut grew under Sunga rule, which complicates this claim.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The Divyavadana calls Pushyamitra a persecutor of Buddhists, but the growth of Sanchi and Bharhut under Sunga rule points the other way.

s: Who founded the Sunga dynasty in Magadha?
x: Pushyamitra Sunga founded the Sunga dynasty after overthrowing the Mauryas.

s: How did Pushyamitra Sunga seize power from the Mauryas?
o: defeating the Indo-Greeks in the north-west
obtaining the throne through a council of ministers
assassinating Brihadratha during an army review
marrying into the Mauryan royal family
x: Pushyamitra, the Mauryan commander-in-chief, killed Brihadratha during a military review, thereby carrying out a military coup.

s: In which year, approximately, was the Sunga dynasty founded?
x: The Sunga dynasty is generally dated to 187 BC, though some accounts give approximately 185 BCE.

s: Pushyamitra Sunga belonged to which gotra and held which position before founding the Sunga dynasty?
x: Pushyamitra Sunga was a Brahmana of the Bharadvaja gotra and served as a senapati.

s: Which inscription refers to the two Ashvamedha sacrifices of Pushyamitra Sunga?
x: Pushyamitra performed two Ashvamedhas, referred to in the Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva.

s: According to Malavikagnimitram, who defeated a Yavana army on the Sindhu river?
x: Malavikagnimitram records that Vasumitra, the grandson of Pushyamitra, defeated a Yavana army on the Sindhu river.

s: Which last Sunga ruler was killed by Vasudeva Kanva, the founder of the Kanva dynasty?
x: Vasudeva Kanva, a Brahmana minister, killed Devabhuti, the last Sunga, and seized power. Vasumitra and Agnimitra were earlier Sungas, and Brihadratha was the last Maurya, killed by Pushyamitra.

s:
Consider the following statements about the end of the Mauryan dynasty:
1. Brihadratha was killed by his senani Pushyamitra at a military review.
2. Vasudeva Kanva, a minister, founded the dynasty that directly followed the Mauryas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Pushyamitra, a senani, killed Brihadratha at a military review; the Sungas, not the Kanvas, directly followed the Mauryas.

s:
Consider the following about the end of the Kanva dynasty:
1. Susharman was overthrown by Menander.
2. Its last ruler was Susharman.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The last Kanva ruler, Susharman, was ended by the Andhras (Satavahanas), not by Menander.

s: Who was regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty?
x: Simuka, also known as Srimukha, is regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty.

s: How many kings ruled in the Kanva dynasty?
x: The Kanvas had four kings – Vasudeva, Bhumimitra, Narayana and Susharman (c. 73–28 BC).

s: Who gave the financial crisis theory of the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
x: Kosambi gave the financial crisis theory; H. P. Shastri gave the Brahmanical reaction theory, Raychaudhuri the pacifism theory and Romila Thapar stressed over-centralisation.

s: Which of the following is cited as evidence of the financial crisis of the later Mauryas?
o: Increase in the purity of silver coins
Debasement of later punch-marked silver coins with more alloy
x: The higher alloy content of later punch-marked silver coins is read as evidence of fiscal strain and debasement.

s: Ashoka's expenditure on which of the following was regarded as a strain on the Mauryan treasury?
o: Dhamma missions and donations to the Sangha
x: Spending on Dhamma missions and donations to the Buddhist Sangha was considered a burden on the treasury.

s: Which historian linked the decline of the Mauryas to a Brahmanical reaction against Ashoka's pro-Buddhist policy?
x: H.P. Shastri held that Ashoka's pro-Buddhist policy and ban on sacrifices angered the Brahmins.

s: Which historian held that over-centralisation and dependence on the king caused the Mauryan collapse?
x: Romila Thapar stressed over-centralisation, with rule depending on the king and weak successors.

s: Which of the following pairs of theory of Mauryan decline and historian is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The financial crisis theory is D.D. Kosambi's; H.P. Shastri gave the Brahmanical reaction theory.

s: The Divyavadana's evidence of revolts against wicked officials at Taxila supports which theory of Mauryan decline?
x: Revolts at Taxila against wicked officials are cited for the oppressive provincial rule theory.

s: Which historian blamed Ashoka's pacifism for the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
x: H.C. Raychaudhuri held that Ashoka's non-violence after Kalinga weakened the army.

s: Which rulers were associated with the western part of the later Mauryan Empire after its division?
x: Kunala and later Samprati were associated with the western part, while Dasharatha through Brihadratha ruled the eastern part.

s: By about which year did the Indo-Greeks virtually supplant the western later Mauryan territories?
x: The Indo-Greeks had virtually replaced the western later Mauryas by about 180 BC.

s: Samprati, a later Mauryan ruler, was a patron of which faith?
x: Samprati, Ashoka's grandson, was a Jain patron who ruled c. 230–215 BCE.

s: With the breakaway of which region was Yajnasena, mentioned in Malavikagnimitram, associated?
x: Yajnasena is associated with Vidarbha in the account of the regions that broke away after Ashoka.

s: How did the construction of the Great Wall of China around 220 BC affect the Mauryan north-west?
o: diverted Scythian tribes westward and southward towards India
forced the Indo-Greeks to migrate to Egypt
ended all contact between China and India
enabled the Mauryas to control Bactria
x: The Great Wall diverted Scythian tribes towards the west and south, increasing pressure on regions near India while Mauryan frontier defence weakened.

s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a factor in the decline of the Mauryan Empire?
o: Weak and oppressive successors after Ashoka
A permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks
x: A permanent alliance with the Indo-Greeks was not a cause of Mauryan decline. Indo-Greek raids and pressure were among the external problems faced by the empire.

s: Which Bactrian (Indo-Greek) rulers threatened the north-west of the Mauryan Empire after Ashoka?
x: Bactrian or Indo-Greek invasions associated with Demetrius and later Menander threatened the north-west after Ashoka.

s: From whom did Antiochus III obtain tribute after crossing the Hindu Kush around 206 BC?
x: Antiochus III crossed the Hindu Kush around 206 BC and took tribute from the local ruler Subhagasena.

s: Which was the capital of Menander (Milinda), the Indo-Greek ruler?
x: Menander ruled from Sagala (Sialkot) and held a dialogue with the monk Nagasena in the Milindapanha.

s: The Milindapanha is a dialogue between the Indo-Greek king Menander and which Buddhist monk?
x: Menander (Milinda), whose capital was Sagala, held a dialogue with the monk Nagasena, recorded in the Milindapanha.

s: By what name do the Jain texts refer to the Andhra country?
x: Stem error: 'Andhakaratta' is the name used in Buddhist literature, not Jain texts; the item needs rewording before it can be keyed.

s: What were the Andhakas, according to the Kathavatthu?
x: The Kathavatthu mentions the Andhakas as a Buddhist school (Third Council).

s: In which Buddhist text is the Andhra region called 'Andhapatha' (Andhra Path)?
x: The Vinayavatthu uses the name Andhapatha; the Kathavatthu speaks of the Andhakas as a school, and the Suttanipata of Assaka and Mulaka.

s: What name do the Pali texts give to the Andhra country on the banks of the Godavari, near where Bavari lived?
x: Pali texts call it Andhakarattha, on the Godavari, near Bavari's hermitage.

s: According to the Chulla-Kalinga Jataka, the king of Assaka (Asmaka) defeated the king of which kingdom?
x: The Chulla-Kalinga Jataka records the Kalinga–Assaka conflict in which the king of Assaka defeated the king of Kalinga.

s: Which Jataka mentions Andhapura (Andhakapura), reached by merchants across the river Telavaha?
x: The Serivanija Jataka describes Andhapura across the Telavaha.

s: In which story of the Aitareya Brahmana does the word 'Andhra' first appear?
x: 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana in connection with the Sunahshepa story, not in the Rig Veda.

s: In which text does the word 'Andhra' first appear?
x: 'Andhra' first appears in the Aitareya Brahmana, in the Sunahshepa story, not in the Rigveda.

s: According to the Mahabharata, on whose side did the Andhras fight?
x: The Mahabharata states that the Andhras sided with the Kauravas.

s: In which text does the word 'Andhra' first occur?
x: The Aitareya Brahmana first mentions the Andhras, in the Sunahshepa story; the Rigveda does not mention them.

s: Megasthenes’ Indica credits the Andhras with which of the following combinations?
o: 50 fortified towns and a standing navy
30 fortified towns and a large army
40 fortified towns and a small navy
20 fortified towns and a large cavalry
x: Megasthenes’ Indica describes the Andhras as possessing 30 fortified towns and a large army.

s: Which edict of Ashoka names the Andhras among the peoples within his empire?
x: Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII names the Andhras among the peoples within his empire. Pillar Edict VII, Minor Rock Edict I and Rock Edict II do not carry this reference.

s: In which story of the Aitareya Brahmana does the first reference to the Andhras occur?
x: The Aitareya Brahmana names the Andhras in the Sunahshepa story.

s: In the Sunahshepa story, who cursed his sons to become Andhras, Pundras and Pulindas?
x: Vishvamitra cursed his fifty sons to become Andhras, Pundras, Pulindas and others.

s: Which of the following texts does NOT mention the Andhras?
x: The Rigveda does not mention the Andhras; the Aitareya Brahmana first names them, and the Mahabharata and Rock Edict XIII also refer to them.

s: Which literary work contains the earliest reference to the Andhras as a people in the story of Sunahshepa?
x: The Aitareya Brahmana gives the earliest literary reference to the Andhras. In the Sunahshepa story, Vishwamitra cursed fifty of his sons to become Andhras, Pundras and Pulindas.

s: According to the Mahabharata, on which side did the Andhras fight?
x: The Mahabharata states that the Andhras fought on the Kaurava side; the Rigveda does not mention them and the Vayu Purana places them in the Deccan.

s: Which of the following texts does NOT mention the Andhras?
x: The Rigveda has no mention of the Andhras; the Aitareya Brahmana gives the first mention.

s: In the Aitareya Brahmana, how many sons of Vishwamitra were cursed to become Andhras, Pundras and Pulindas?
x: In the Sunahshepa story Vishwamitra cursed his 50 sons.

s: Who was the first to mention forts in Andhra?
x: Megasthenes, in the Indica, first mentioned walled towns (forts) of the Andhras.

s: According to Megasthenes, the Andhras had how many walled towns?
x: Megasthenes counted 30 walled towns with walls and towers in Andhra.

s:
Consider the following statements about Megasthenes' account of the Andhras:
1. The Andhra king had 1,00,000 infantry.
2. The Andhra king had 1,000 elephants.
3. Megasthenes was the ambassador of Antiochus III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Andhra army had 1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 elephants; Megasthenes was the ambassador of Seleucus.

s: By which writer is Megasthenes' report of the Andhra king's army preserved?
x: Megasthenes' report of 1,00,000 infantry, 2,000 cavalry and 1,000 elephants of the Andhra king is preserved by Pliny.

s: With which place is Andhranagari or Dhanyakataka identified?
x: Andhranagari, also called Dhanyakataka, is identified with Amaravati-Dharanikota on the Krishna River. The river identification is associated with P. C. Ray.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sriparvata (Vijayapuri) is Nagarjunakonda. The Siddharthaka chaitya is placed at Gudivada (APPSC G2 2008 key; some lists give Guntupalli), not Bodhan, the Assaka capital. Andhranagari (Dhanyakataka) is Amaravati-Dharanikota, and the Rajagirika centre is Guntupalli.

s: With which modern place is the Siddharthaka chaitya of Buddhist literature identified?
x: The Siddharthaka chaitya is identified with Gudivada in Krishna district.

s: Dhanyakataka (Amaravati-Dharanikota) was the capital of which dynasty in its later phase?
x: Dhanyakataka, a Mahasanghika Buddhist centre, was the capital of the later Satavahanas.

s: Which early historic site in Krishna district shows continuous occupation from Mauryan to Satavahana times?
x: Gudiwada Dibba in Krishna district is an early historic mound showing continuous occupation from Mauryan to Satavahana times.

s: Of which tradition was Adurru in East Godavari district an important centre?
x: Adurru in East Godavari district was a Mahasanghika Buddhist centre.

s: The stupa excavated at Vaddamanu near Amaravati belongs to which religion?
x: Vaddamanu has a Jain stupa with label inscriptions of Jain teachers.

s: What was Gottiprolu, excavated by the ASI in the Nellore region, mainly?
o: Trade centre within a massive brick wall
x: Gottiprolu was a large 2nd–1st c. BCE trade settlement enclosed by a massive brick wall near an ancient seaport.

s: Which early historic site in the Nellore region was declared a Monument of National Importance in July 2026?
x: Gottiprolu, a walled trade centre of the 2nd-1st c. BCE excavated by the ASI, was declared a Monument of National Importance in July 2026.

s: Which of the following is true of the date of the Dharanikota sculptures?
o: Later than those of Sanchi and Bharhut
Older than those of Sanchi and Bharhut
x: Dharanikota sculptures, in the Amaravati region, are described as older than those of Sanchi and Bharhut.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Mulaka had its capital at Pratishthana; Assaka (also called Asmaka) had its capital at Bodhan, and Andhra lay on the Dakshinapatha route.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about early Andhra?
o: Andhra formed part of the Dakshinapatha trade route
Andhra lay outside the major trade routes
Andhra merchant guilds later used Masulipatnam
x: Andhra lay on the Dakshinapatha trade route, so it was not outside the major trade routes; its guilds used Kalingapatnam and later Masulipatnam.

s: Which was the capital of Mulaka, the neighbour of Assaka?
x: Mulaka's capital was Pratishthana.

s: Which was the capital of the Assaka (Asmaka) janapada?
x: Assaka on the Godavari had its capital at Bodhan (Podana); Pratishthana was the capital of Mulaka.

s: According to the Bavari legend, how many disciples were sent to the Buddha?
x: Bavari sent sixteen disciples to meet the Buddha. The episode is preserved in the Suttanipata, in the Parayana-vagga.

s: From where did Bavari, who settled in Assaka territory on the Godavari, originally come?
x: Bavari was a Brahmin teacher from Kosala who settled on the Godavari in Assaka territory.

s: According to the Bavari legend, when did Buddhist ideas reach the Godavari region?
x: The Bavari legend indicates that Buddhist ideas had reached the Godavari region before Mauryan expansion.

s: In which Buddhist text is the story of Bavari sending sixteen disciples to the Buddha found?
x: Bavari's story is in the Parayana-vagga of the Suttanipata, not in the Jatakas.

s: What was the significance of the Mauryan phase for Buddhism in Andhra?
o: Led to Buddhism's disappearance from Andhra
Made Buddhism institutional in the region
x: The Mauryan phase made Buddhism institutional in Andhra.

s: Who is associated with the first Buddhist teaching mission to Andhra and the enshrinement of Buddha’s bone relics at Amaravati?
x: Ashoka sent Mahadeva Bhikshu to Amaravati. He is regarded as the first Buddhist teacher in Andhra and is associated with enshrining Buddha’s bone relics there.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ashokan inscriptions in Andhra?
o: Erragudi is in present Nandyal district
Rajula Mandagiri has a fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict
The Erragudi inscription is in Prakrit language and Brahmi script
The Erragudi edict asks teachers to inculcate Dhamma in pupils
x: Rajula Mandagiri has a minor edict; the pillar-edict fragment is at Amaravati. The statements on Erragudi are correct.

s: What does the Ashokan edict at Erragudi direct?
o: Teachers must inculcate Dhamma in their pupils
Animal sacrifice be banned at Ujjain
Dhamma Mahamattas be sent to Sri Lanka
x: The Erragudi edict says teachers must inculcate Dhamma (religious thought) in pupils and appoints Rajukas.

s: What type of Ashokan inscription is found at Rajula Mandagiri in Kurnool?
x: Rajula Mandagiri has an Ashokan minor edict, not a pillar edict; Amaravati has a pillar fragment.

s: At which place in Andhra Pradesh was a fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict found?
x: Amaravati has a fragment of an Ashokan pillar edict; Erragudi and Rajula Mandagiri have rock edicts.

s: According to the Puranic tradition, which dynasties were defeated by the Satavahanas?
x: The Puranas state that the Satavahanas defeated the Sunga and Kanva dynasties.

s: The Shunga dynasty ruled approximately during which period?
x: The Sungas ruled from the killing of Brihadratha (187 BC in the notes, often given as about 185 BCE) until Vasudeva Kanva killed Devabhuti (about 75-73 BCE). So 185 BCE-73 BCE is the closest option.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty?
x: Devabhuti was the last Shunga ruler; he was killed by his minister Vasudeva Kanva.

s: Which dynasty immediately preceded the Nanda Dynasty in Magadha?
x: The Nanda dynasty replaced the Shishunaga dynasty in Magadha, Mahapadma Nanda having overthrown the last Shishunaga king. The Haryankas came before the Shishunagas; the Mauryas and Shungas came after the Nandas.

s: Which of the following dynastic successions in Magadha is NOT correct?
x: The Mauryas came before the Kanvas; the order was Maurya, Shunga, Kanva, and the Nandas followed the Shishunagas.

s: Who founded the Kanva dynasty by overthrowing the last Shunga king?
x: Vasudeva Kanva overthrew the last Shunga king and began the Kanva dynasty.

s:
Consider the following statements about the traditional accounts of the post-Mauryan period:
1. Satakarni I is said to have defeated Pushyamitra Sunga.
2. Simuka is associated with ending the Sunga dynasty.
3. Vasumitra is linked with the defeat of the Yavanas on the Sindhu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Satakarni I is said to have defeated Pushyamitra and Vasumitra beat the Yavanas on the Sindhu; Simuka ended the Kanva dynasty, not the Sunga.

s: In the sequence Maurya – Sunga – Kanva – ____, which dynasty fills the blank?
x: The chronological order of rule is Maurya, Sunga, Kanva and Kushana.

s: Which founder is correctly matched with the ruler he replaced?
x: Vasudeva Kanva replaced Devabhuti; Pushyamitra replaced Brihadratha Maurya and Simuka replaced Susharma.

s: Who overthrew Susharman, the last Kanva ruler?
x: Simuka, founder of the Satavahana dynasty, overthrew Susharman and ended the Kanva dynasty.

s: Which ruler is called Sarvakshatrantaka in the Puranas?
x: The Puranas call Mahapadma Nanda (Ugrasen) Sarvakshatrantaka and Aparoparashurama.

s: Which powerful feudatories rose during the Sunga period?
x: Bhojas, Maharathis and Rastrikas rose as powerful feudatories, while the Sungas broadly kept Mauryan administrative institutions.

s: How did the Manusmriti, which took its early shape in the Sunga period, classify foreigners?
x: The Manusmriti took early shape in this period and classified foreigners as Vratya Kshatriyas.

s: The Sungas belonged to which varna?
x: The Sungas were Brahmins, with their heartland in Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley.

s: The Sunga court encouraged a revival of which language, in contrast to Ashoka's use of Prakrit?
x: The Sunga court encouraged a revival of classical Sanskrit, whereas Ashoka had used Prakrit.

s: Which region formed the heartland of the Sunga kingdom?
o: Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley
x: The Sunga heartland was Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley; the north-west went to the Yavanas.

s: Which text records Pushyamitra killing Brihadratha while showing him the army?
x: The Harshacharita records Pushyamitra killing Brihadratha during an army review; Malavikagnimitram records Vasumitra's victory over the Yavanas.

s: Which of the following about Pushyamitra Shunga is NOT correct?
o: Patanjali is linked with his Ashvamedha ceremonies
The Ayodhya inscription records his two Ashvamedhas
He was a senapati before founding the dynasty
x: Pushyamitra performed two, not three, Ashvamedha yajnas, as the Ayodhya inscription records.

s:
The Sunga period is associated with:
1. Brahmanical revival
2. The rise of Bhagavatism
3. The development of stone Buddhist art
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: The Sunga period saw Brahmanical revival, the rise of Bhagavatism and the development of stone Buddhist art.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The ancestors of the Sungas came from Ujjain.
2. Agnimitra, son of Pushyamitra, was viceroy at Vidisha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are true: the Sunga ancestors came from Ujjain, and Agnimitra governed Vidisha for his father.

s: Pushyamitra's hostility towards Buddhism was probably aimed at monasteries allied with which power?
x: Hostility was probably aimed at monasteries allied with the Indo-Greeks, while merchants and guilds kept funding Buddhism.

s: The tradition concerning the destruction of the original Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya is associated with which two rulers?
o: Pushyamitra Sunga and Shashanka of Gauda
x: One tradition attributes destruction of the original Bodhi Tree to Pushyamitra and also records a similar act by Shashanka of Gauda in the seventh century CE.

s: What is the main theme of Visakhadatta's Mudrarakshasa?
o: The Satavahana conquest of the Deccan
x: Mudrarakshasa concerns Chandragupta Maurya and the establishment of Mauryan power, so it is not used for the Yavana invasion in Pushyamitra's reign.

s: The Yavana advance on Saketa, Panchala, Mathura and Pataliputra is described in which source?
x: The Gargi Samhita records the Yavana advance on Saketa, Panchala, Mathura and Pataliputra.

s: Agnimitra, a prominent Sunga ruler, is associated with which of the following developments?
o: Receiving the Besnagar pillar from Heliodorus
Defeating the Yavanas on the Sindhu
x: Agnimitra is noted for fighting Yajnasena of Vidarbha. The defeat of the Yavanas on the Sindhu is associated with Vasumitra, while the other alternatives refer to different historical contexts.

s: Which Buddhist text, along with Taranatha, portrays Pushyamitra Sunga as a persecutor of Buddhists?
x: Divyavadana and Taranatha portray Pushyamitra as a persecutor; Romila Thapar and Lamotte regard this account as exaggerated and sectarian.

s: Which text describes the Yavana siege of Saketa and Madhyamika?
x: Patanjali's Mahabhashya records the Yavana siege of Saketa and Madhyamika.

s: Who is the author of the Gargi Samhita (Yuga Purana)?
x: The Gargi Samhita is by Garga and describes the Yavana march to Pataliputra.

s: Who is the author of Mrichchhakatikam?
x: Mrichchhakatikam is by Sudraka; Malavikagnimitram is by Kalidasa and Mahabhashya by Patanjali.

s: Who is the author of the Harshacharita, which says that Pushyamitra killed Brihadratha while showing him the army?
x: Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita; Kalidasa wrote Malavikagnimitram and Patanjali the Mahabhashya.

s: Heliodorus came to the court of which Sunga ruler?
x: Heliodorus came to Bhagabhadra's court; Agnimitra was viceroy at Vidisha and Vasumitra defeated the Yavanas on the Sindhu.

s: Where did Agnimitra, son of Pushyamitra, serve as viceroy?
x: Agnimitra was viceroy at Vidisha and fought Yajnasena of Vidarbha.

s: How was Vasumitra, who defeated the Yavanas, related to Pushyamitra?
x: Vasumitra was Agnimitra's son and so Pushyamitra's grandson.

s: How many acts does Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram have?
x: Malavikagnimitram, Kalidasa's first play, has 5 acts.

s: Which was the first play of Kalidasa?
x: Malavikagnimitram, the love story of Agnimitra and Malavika in 5 acts, was Kalidasa's first play.

s: Patanjali's Mahabhashya comments on which work, through Katyayana's Varttikas?
x: The Mahabhashya comments on Panini's Ashtadhyayi through Katyayana's Varttikas - the Panini-Katyayana-Patanjali grammarian trio.

s: In what capacity is Patanjali believed to have served Pushyamitra Sunga?
x: Patanjali is believed to have been Pushyamitra's royal priest and supervised his two Ashvamedhas.

s: Whose ambassador was Heliodorus when he erected the Besnagar pillar?
x: Heliodorus was the ambassador of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas at the court of the Sunga king Bhagabhadra.

s: Of which city was Heliodorus, who erected the Besnagar pillar, a native?
x: Heliodorus was from Taxila; the pillar stands at Besnagar near Vidisha, with an inscription in Prakrit and Brahmi.

s: What is the Besnagar pillar?
x: The Besnagar monument is a Garuda-dhvaja dedicated to Vasudeva, and Heliodorus describes himself as a Bhagavata.

s: What is the main historical significance of the Besnagar pillar?
o: The earliest use of iron in the Ganga valley
The establishment of the Kanva dynasty
Early Bhagavatism and the absorption of a foreigner into an Indian religious tradition
x: The pillar is early inscriptional evidence of Bhagavatism, an early form of Vaishnavism, and shows the assimilation of a foreigner into an Indian religious tradition.

s: Where is the Heliodorus (Garuda) pillar located?
x: Heliodorus set up the Garuda-dhvaja to Vasudeva at Besnagar (Bhilsa/Vidisha) in Madhya Pradesh.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gupta rulers – Tamil devotees of Vishnu
x: Heliodorus set up the Garuda pillar at Besnagar as a Bhagavata; the Alvars worshipped Vishnu, the Nayanars Shiva, and the Gupta kings took the title Parama-bhagavata.

s: To which ruler does the inscription of Ananda on the south torana of Sanchi link it?
